text:
jordan (Instacorp): Hey team — after your scheduled IdP cert rotation last night we started getting SSO failures for ~30% of our users. They see a 500 from our SP when we hit /saml/acs. Can you confirm what changed on Redwood's side?

alex_chen: Sorry you're hitting that, Jordan. We did a rotation for the IdP cert you provided at 2026-03-03T02:15Z. Quick Q: are you using the metadata URL or did you upload static XML to your SP config?

jordan (Instacorp): We host metadata at https://idp.instacorp.com/metadata.xml, we didn't touch our SP. The timing matches. Errors in our logs: `SAMLResponse invalid_signature` and sometimes `AudienceRestriction mismatch`.

maria_ops: Can you paste an example SAML Response (base64) or the decoded assertion snippet (remove PII)? Also check whether your ACS URL includes a trailing slash — we've seen that cause Audience mismatch with some IdPs.

jordan (Instacorp): Pasted a redacted assertion (decoded):

```
<Assertion xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">
  <Issuer>https://idp.instacorp.com/</Issuer>
  <Subject>...</Subject>
  <Conditions>
    <AudienceRestriction>
      <Audience>https://app.redwood-inference.com</Audience>
    </AudienceRestriction>
  </Conditions>
  <Signature>...signature blob...</Signature>
</Assertion>
```

jordan (Instacorp): Our SP ACS is https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs (no trailing slash).

alex_chen: Thanks. Couple of things we'll check: 1) whether IdP metadata served the new cert and if it included multiple KeyDescriptor entries (old + new), 2) if EntityID/Issuer normalization changed (trailing slash), 3) our SP accepted the new cert fingerprint.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: IdP certs updated in prod: idp.instacorp.com metadata fetched at 2026-03-03T02:18:07Z (SHA256 fingerprint a1:2b:3c:...).

maria_ops: Jordan — can you run `openssl` against the metadata cert you host and paste the fingerprint you see? Example command:

```
# fetch cert from metadata and show fingerprint
curl -s https://idp.instacorp.com/metadata.xml | xmllint --xpath "(//ds:X509Certificate)[1]" - 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p' | base64 -d > /tmp/idp.crt
openssl x509 -in /tmp/idp.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256
```

jordan (Instacorp): Ran it, got: `SHA256 Fingerprint=a1:2B:3C:4D:5E:6F:7A:8B:9C:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:11`

alex_chen: That matches the fingerprint our deploy log showed. Two likely causes: the IdP replaced the cert but didn't include the previous cert in metadata (so some IdP nodes still sign with the old cert), or the Assertion Issuer value includes a trailing slash while our SP expects no trailing slash (Issuer normalization mismatch). The mixed failure ratio (~30%) hints at multi-node IdP with rolling certs.

jordan (Instacorp): Ah — our IdP is a cluster; we rotated certs but maybe a few nodes still sign with the old key. How do we confirm?

maria_ops: You can decode several SAMLResponses from failing users and check the Signature's KeyInfo X509Certificate fingerprint; that will tell you which cert signed the response. Example: decode base64, find `<X509Certificate>` text, base64-decode and fingerprint. If you see two different fingerprints across responses, that's the cause.

jordan (Instacorp): I decoded two failures; one signed with fingerprint `...FF:00` and another with `...EE:11` (old/new). So yes, mixed signing.

alex_chen: Ok that explains intermittent invalid_signature errors. Short term workarounds: 1) Upload both certs (old + new) into our SP trust store so we accept either signature. 2) Reconfigure IdP to publish dual-key metadata (both KeyDescriptor nodes) during rotation.

jordan (Instacorp): How do I upload both certs to Redwood? We only have a single field in the console for IdP cert.

maria_ops: For now we can add the old cert on the backend for your org. Send both PEMs to a secure upload (support artifact link) or paste fingerprints & we can confirm. We'll also add a note to the console to support multiple KeyDescriptors.

jordan (Instacorp): Uploaded both PEMs to the secure artifact link. Also noticed our metadata didn't include `WantAuthnRequestsSigned` change. Could that break anything?

alex_chen: That generally affects IdP accepting SP-initiated authnrequests; not the Response signature verification. Not likely the cause here.

maria_ops: We added the old cert to your org's trust store at 2026-03-03T03:02Z. Can you verify the failing users can log in now?

jordan (Instacorp): Testing — two previously failing users can login now. Huge relief, thank you.

alex_chen: Great. Postmortem items for us: add support for multi-key metadata in the UI, improve error message for signature failures to show expected vs actual fingerprint (sanitized), and doc a recommended rotation pattern: publish dual certs, wait 48h for propagation, then remove old cert.

maria_ops: Also adding temporary checklist: set clock skew to 5m on SP if you see NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter errors, and verify Audience matches exactly (scheme + host + path if ACS is used as audience).

jordan (Instacorp): One follow-up — can you add a note to our org settings that indicates which fingerprint is currently primary? Would help during future rotations.

alex_chen: Yep, we can add an org-level metadata view that shows all accepted fingerprints + upload history. We'll follow up in a short RFC.

oncall-bot: ticket #SUP-81922 updated — resolution: added old cert to trust store, observed immediate reduction in failures.

jordan (Instacorp): Thanks everyone. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :heart:
